title: API 653 Training in Tulsa, OK: Tank Inspector Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 653 exam prep for Tulsa and Cushing tank inspectors: crude terminals, breakout tanks, refinery tanks and Oklahoma rules, with instructor Q&A.
h1: API 653 Training in Tulsa: Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector Exam Prep for Cushing Terminals and Tulsa Tank Farms
html:
API 653 exam prep for tank inspectors between Tulsa and Cushing

The country between Tulsa and Cushing holds a great deal of aboveground storage. Cushing is the crude hub where NYMEX WTI futures contracts settle, Tulsa has a refinery with its own tank farms, and ONEOK, which has its headquarters in Tulsa, added a large storage business when it completed its acquisition of the Tulsa-based Magellan Midstream Partners in September 2023. ONEOK's announcement described Magellan as able to store more than 100 million barrels of petroleum products across its system. Tank inspection is steady work here, and this page is for the people preparing to do it as certified API 653 inspectors.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Tulsa or Cushing. The API 653 course is online and self-paced, and an instructor answers questions as you work through it, so you can study between terminal shifts and tank outages. API sets the eligibility rules in Annex D of API 653, administers the examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification. Atlantis is not an API-approved provider of training, and the course is preparation, not a certificate.

Cushing, the tank hub west of Tulsa

Cushing lies in Payne County, and Tulsa International Airport is about 59 miles to its east-north-east. The Oklahoma Historical Society records that its old pipeline terminal, with 39 storage tanks and pipelines able to move up to 1.5 million barrels a day, helped earn the town its nickname, Pipeline Crossroads of the World. Today Enbridge describes Cushing as a major crude storage hub and the site of NYMEX WTI contract settlement.

Figures for storage at Cushing date quickly, so treat each one with its date. EIA, writing in September 2021, put Cushing's working storage capacity at 76.6 million barrels, and the agency has since stopped publishing its storage capacity report, the last edition of which covered March 2024. Enbridge lists 27 million barrels of contract storage at Cushing in operation or under construction, including a 34-tank facility of about 6.6 million barrels that it bought from Blueknight Energy Partners in 2021. TankTerminals.com listed 16 storage terminals at Cushing in November 2023.

For a candidate, the point is the kind of tank. Storage at Cushing is mostly large welded crude tanks of the kind API 650 covers, and external floating roofs are common in crude service. Those tanks go through out-of-service internal inspections, floor scans, bottom repairs and settlement surveys, which is the work the API 653 examination is built around.

Tanks in Tulsa itself

HF Sinclair's Tulsa refinery has its own storage for crude, intermediates moving between its two plants, and finished products, which the company says are marketed to the Mid-Continent states. The specialty side adds tanks of a different character. EIA lists asphalt production capacity of 9,900 barrels per stream day at Tulsa West, and HF Sinclair says the site produces base oils, specialty process oils, horticultural oils, asphalt modifiers and wax, sold worldwide through terminals and a North American distributor network. Heated asphalt and wax tanks bring insulated shells, heating coils and elevated operating temperatures into the inspection, which makes corrosion under insulation and the condition of the coils part of a refinery tank inspector's routine in a way they rarely are at a crude terminal.

Which rules send an API 653 inspector to an Oklahoma tank

Several overlapping rules decide whether a tank needs a formal API 653 inspection and how its intervals are set. The table summarises the ones a Tulsa or Cushing inspector meets most.

TankRuleWhat it asks
Aboveground storage tanks regulated by the Corporation CommissionOAC 165:26, in the version effective from October 2023Adopts API 653, Fifth Edition (2014), with Addendum 1 (2018) and Addendum 2 (2020), by reference; requires compliance with EPA's SPCC rule; requires cathodic protection to be tested within six months of installation or repair and then at least every three years, with impressed current systems checked every 60 days
Bulk storage containers at a facility with an SPCC plan40 CFR 112.8(c)(6)Integrity testing or inspection on a regular schedule and whenever material repairs are made, with personnel qualifications set by industry standards; EPA says formal API 653 inspections are conducted by an API 653 certified inspector
Atmospheric and low-pressure steel breakout tanks on a pipeline system49 CFR 195.432(b)Physical integrity assessed according to API 653, but its risk-based alternative internal inspection interval may not be used
Pressurised breakout tanks built to API 251049 CFR 195.432(c)Inspection according to section 6 of API 510, not API 653
Other in-service breakout tanks49 CFR 195.432(a)Inspection at least once each calendar year at intervals not exceeding 15 months; this paragraph excludes tanks inspected under (b) and (c)
Tanks used in oil and gas exploration or productionOAC 165:26-1-22(a)(1)Excluded from the Corporation Commission's aboveground tank rules altogether

One change is pending. In June 2026 PHMSA proposed allowing RBI to set breakout tank internal intervals, capped at 20 years for the first internal inspection and 25 years for later ones. It is a proposal, not a final rule, so the current text of 195.432 still applies. These regulations are not among the publications the examination lists, which centre on API 653, API 650 and the documents examined with them. Atlantis's note on who may inspect tanks under SPCC covers the federal side in more detail.

Worked example: what a heavier crude does to the fill height

Cushing tanks change grades, and a tank that switches to a denser crude must be checked again even if nothing about the steel has changed. API 653 4.3.3.1 gives the minimum thickness of a whole shell course as tmin = 2.6 (H − 1) D G ÷ (S E). Rearranged, the maximum liquid height above the bottom of that course is H = (S E t) ÷ (2.6 D G) + 1, where t is the thickness that will remain at the next inspection.

Take a 180-ft diameter crude tank whose first course is expected to have 0.60 in. left at the next inspection. Use the lower-course allowable stress API 653 gives for unknown material, 23,600 psi, and assume E = 1.0 for this illustration.

  • Light crude, G = 0.83: H = (23,600 × 1.0 × 0.60) ÷ (2.6 × 180 × 0.83) + 1 = 14,160 ÷ 388.44 + 1 = 37.45 ft.
  • Heavier crude, G = 0.93: H = 14,160 ÷ 435.24 + 1 = 33.53 ft.

The change of grade costs almost 4 ft of fill height on the first course alone. Now repeat for the second course, whose height is measured from the bottom of that course. If it is 8 ft tall and will have 0.50 in. left, then H = (23,600 × 0.50) ÷ 435.24 + 1 = 28.11 ft above its own bottom, or 36.11 ft above the tank bottom, so the first course still governs at 33.53 ft. The exam gives you the formulas; it tests whether you take S from the right row, measure H from the right place and remember that no course may be thinner than 0.1 in. The guide to API 653 shell minimum thickness sets out the rules behind each term.

Floors, floating roofs and Oklahoma weather

The floor is where a crude tank usually loses most metal, and it is the part nobody can see in service. Product-side pitting under water and sediment and soil-side corrosion where cathodic protection is weak both show up on floor scans, and the Corporation Commission's cathodic protection testing rules make the soil side a regular subject for owners. The examination asks how the bottom is evaluated and what minimum remaining thickness is acceptable, which depends on whether the tank has a means of detecting and containing a leak; read the release prevention barrier note alongside those clauses.

External floating roofs carry their own list: pontoons, seals, deck plates, roof supports and the drains that carry rainwater off the roof. Oklahoma's heavy spring rain tests roof drains and pontoon buoyancy, summer heat bakes seals, and winter cold can freeze water in drain lines and water draws. None of that is examined as weather, but floating roof inspection is, and the floating roof guide describes what an inspector checks.

Routes into API 653 for Tulsa and Cushing tank people

Annex D of API 653 sets the experience required. A bachelor's degree in engineering or technology needs one year of supervising or performing inspection of aboveground storage tanks. A two-year degree or certificate needs two years and a high school diploma three, in design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of tanks, including one year of inspection, and without formal education the requirement is five years or more. Experience must be from the last ten years, gained while employed by or under contract with an authorized inspection agency. The API 653 certification page explains how to document it.

  • Terminal operations and maintenance staff. People who run tank farms at Cushing know the tanks well; operation counts toward the total, and the year of inspection is usually what remains.
  • Tank construction and repair crews. Welders, fitters and quality staff on new tanks and bottom replacements learn API 650 at first hand. If you are on the welding inspection side, the AWS CWI exam prep for Tulsa is a separate course worth considering.
  • NDT technicians. Floor scanning, UT thickness surveys and weld examination put technicians close to the inspector's decisions. Atlantis's NDT training in Tulsa covers the ASNT methods those roles use.
  • Engineers. Engineers at terminal operators and tank contractors reach the exam soonest, once they have a year of inspection.

Studying API 653 around terminal and outage work

Out-of-service tank inspections come in bursts, and a candidate who works them can lose weeks of study at a time. Use the quieter stretches for the reading that the closed-book half depends on: API 653 itself, RP 575 and the relevant sections of RP 571. Keep the open-book practice, mostly in API 650, for shorter sessions, and learn where the shell design, bottom, annular plate and impact-test rules sit so you can reach them quickly on a PDF. Send questions to the instructor when a calculation does not come out rather than waiting for a quieter week.

Prometric lists test centres in and around Tulsa, so a candidate based in Cushing can choose one by drive time. Book as soon as API confirms your eligibility. The API 653 practice questions are a quick way to find your weak areas before the timed papers.

Sponsoring tank inspectors from a Cushing terminal or Tulsa contractor

Terminal operators and tank contractors can enrol one candidate or a group, and fees are quoted on request. With no class days to attend, a sponsored inspector keeps covering the tank farm while preparing, and each candidate applies to API individually with their own experience record. The employer's part is to confirm that experience and to plan around the exam day. Atlantis's page on API 653 tank inspection support in Oklahoma describes the NDE it performs for owners' inspectors, a service separate from the course.

faq.q: Is there an API 653 course I can attend in Tulsa or Cushing?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Tulsa or Cushing; the API 653 course runs online, at your own pace, with an instructor answering your questions as you go. The examination is held in person at Prometric test centres, and Prometric lists centres in and around Tulsa. API administers the exam and issues the certification to those who pass.

faq.q: Does Oklahoma require an API 653 certified inspector for terminal tanks?
faq.a: The Corporation Commission's aboveground storage tank rules adopt API 653 by reference and require owners to comply with EPA's SPCC rule. Under SPCC, tanks are tested or inspected for integrity on a regular schedule using industry standards, and EPA says formal inspections under API 653 are conducted by an API 653 certified inspector. Owners may use STI SP001 for tanks it covers, so the answer depends on the tank and the standard chosen.

faq.q: Can a breakout tank at Cushing use API 653's risk-based internal interval?
faq.a: Not under the current federal rule. Section 195.432(b) requires breakout tanks to be assessed according to API 653 but excludes its risk-based alternative for setting the internal inspection interval. PHMSA proposed in June 2026 to allow RBI with ceilings of 20 and 25 years, but that is a proposal and has not replaced the rule. Terminal tanks that are not part of a pipeline system are treated differently.

faq.q: Are pressurised breakout tanks inspected to API 653?
faq.a: No. Under 49 CFR 195.432(c), steel aboveground breakout tanks built to API 2510, the standard for pressurised LPG storage, are inspected according to section 6 of API 510. API 653 covers atmospheric and low-pressure steel tanks. The yearly inspection in 195.432(a) applies to breakout tanks that are not inspected under paragraphs (b) or (c).

faq.q: Oklahoma's rule adopts the Fifth Edition of API 653. Is that the edition on my exam?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The Corporation Commission's rules adopt a stated edition, with its 2018 and 2020 addenda, for regulatory purposes. The examination follows the Publications Effectivity Sheet that API issues for each exam window, which names the editions of API 653, API 650 and the other publications examined. Study the editions on your window's sheet, and use the edition your employer and regulator require at work.

faq.q: Does tank construction or repair experience count toward API 653?
faq.a: Yes, on the two-year degree, high school and no formal education routes, Annex D counts experience in the design, construction, repair, operation or inspection of aboveground storage tanks, provided it includes at least one year of inspection work. With an engineering bachelor's degree the requirement is a year of inspection. The experience must fall within the last ten years and be documented on your application, which API verifies.

faq.q: How hard is it to reach a test centre from Cushing?
faq.a: Prometric's locator shows the centres open for API examinations, and Prometric lists centres in and around Tulsa, so a Cushing-based candidate can usually choose by drive time. Book as soon as API accepts your application rather than waiting until the window opens. Plan the day around the full examination, which runs for most of a working day with a lunch break between the closed-book and open-book parts.

faq.q: Can a Cushing terminal enrol several tank inspectors at once?
faq.a: Yes. A terminal operator can enrol a group, and fees are quoted on request. Each inspector studies at their own pace around shift work, sends questions to the instructor when needed and applies to API individually. Because nobody has to leave the terminal for class days, cover is needed only for the exam itself.
